## Executive Signals
- OpenAI has reportedly closed the first $11 billion of a new round at a $1.25 trillion valuation — below its own targets — while Anthropic's IPO chatter slid to roughly $1.2–1.3 trillion (Section 6).
- No frontier model shipped over the weekend: Alibaba's coding tool Qoder quietly slipped in an unnamed stealth model, "Qoduck," and Japan's Shizuku AI announced an 80 ms full-duplex voice model (Section 1).
- Google DeepMind says its AI agents, working under human cryptanalysts, found two faster attacks on legacy 1024-bit RSA; modern 2048-bit keys stay safe (Backfill — Section 2).
- Chainalysis said a "multifront" attack that included AI agents exposed credentials and live tokens for all of its customers (Section 6).
- Trump told CBS's 60 Minutes that AI risks are manageable and he accepts guardrails in principle, but not rules that put the US behind China (Section 5).

## 5. AI Leader and Industry Watch
- **Donald Trump, US president (2026-11-08):** On CBS's 60 Minutes he said AI risks are manageable and that he does not mind guardrails in principle, but will not accept rules that put the United States "in a deep second position" behind China. No bill text accompanied the remarks, and Reuters attributed the reporting to journalist Jarrett Renshaw. Sources: [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/trump-60-minutes-ai-guardrails-china-lead-november-2026).
- **Yao Shunyu, Tencent Hunyuan (2026-11-08):** Warned that frontier models' biology capabilities may soon cross a harm threshold and that open-weight releases such as Tencent's Hy4 need stronger safety work. Source: [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/tencent-yao-shunyu-ai-biology-harm-threshold-hy4-open-weights-2026).
- **Alex Stamos, Cognition (2026-11-07):** In a Decoder interview he argued that open-weight AI can now automate most attack steps and that breach chains have become routine, so defenders must cut security-operations costs and rewrite unsafe code rather than only hunt bugs. Sources: [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/alex-stamos-decoder-ai-cybersecurity-dark-age-november-2026) · [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1029038/ai-cybersecurity-hackers-data-breach-dark-age-alex-stamos).
- **Richard Sutton (2026-11-08):** In a November post he argued that compute alone will not deliver intelligence — widely read as a warning that scaling transformers without new learning methods eventually hits a wall. Source: [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/richard-sutton-bitter-lesson-llm-scaling-debate-november-2026).

## 6. Other Material AI Industry News
- **2026-11-06 (Backfill) — OpenAI closes the first $11 billion of a round at a $1.25 trillion valuation:** Bloomberg reported the initial close, with Reuters naming SoftBank and MGX among investors and Coatue and T. Rowe Price joining. The round could reach about $20 billion — short of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, and below the $1.5 trillion it first sought. Reported, not a completed round. Sources: [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/openai-secures-11-billion-funding-125-trillion-valuation-bloomberg-news-reports-2026-11-06/) · [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/06/openai-reportedly-raises-an-additional-11-billion-at-a-1-25-trillion-valuation/) · [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1029380/openai-1-25-trillion-investment-valuation).
- **2026-11-07 — Anthropic IPO valuation talk slips to about $1.2–1.3 trillion:** Amid a post-election AI-stock rout, Bloomberg reported prospective buyers discussing roughly $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion (some as low as about $1.1 trillion), down from roughly $2 trillion floated in early October. Anthropic's amended S-1 still has no price range, and no decisions are final. Reported, not confirmed. Sources: [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/anthropic-ipo-valuation-expectations-pressured-after-ai-rout) · [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/11/07/anthropic-ipo-valuation-talk-falls-to-13-trillion-after-the-ai-stock-rout/).
- **2026-11-07 — Chainalysis says a multifront attack exposed credentials for all customers:** The blockchain-analytics firm told customers that names, usernames, password hashes and live session tokens for all users were exposed in an incident that included AI agents and an on-path data interception, prompting shutdowns of some services. Sources: [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/chainalysis-says-hackers-stole-credentials-and-tokens-for-all-of-its-customers/) · [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/chainalysis-breach-exposes-all-users.html) · [Chainalysis](https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/security-incident-october-30/).

## Editorial Notes
- **Recovery items (before START_UTC):** Two — OpenAI's $11 billion first close (original date 2026-11-06, Section 6) and Google DeepMind's 1024-bit RSA cryptanalysis (2026-11-06, Section 2). Both were absent from the two most recent briefings and are labelled Backfill. Every other item was first announced or materially updated inside 2026-11-07T06:46:48Z–2026-11-09T06:46:48Z.
- **Weekend research cadence:** The primary window fell on a weekend, and arXiv lists papers only on working days, so the preprints in Section 2 carry 4–6 November posting dates and represent the research front that surfaced during the window rather than items first posted inside it.
- **Reported, not confirmed:** OpenAI's $11 billion is a first close of an open round per Bloomberg, not a completed raise; Anthropic's IPO has no price range and the $1.2–1.3 trillion figures are buyer talks. Chainalysis's exposure counts are the company's own. Qoduck's maker, size, context window and benchmarks are all undisclosed.
- **Vendor claims:** Shizuku-Duplex's turn-taking and quality scores are Shizuku AI's own, judged in part by an LLM (Claude Opus 5.5); its weights and hosting are not part of the announcement. Drex, SAE-Interprets-MoE, TailSteer, Harness-S and EvoMemState numbers are the authors' own.
- **Project metrics:** Star and download counts come from third-party trackers read 2026-11-07/08 UTC and move quickly; entries marked "See repo" have licenses we could not verify.
- **Verified but trimmed under limits:** Meta paused its new commercial terms after publisher and regulatory pushback (2026-11-06); the US AI safety center, CAISSI, now has staff reporting informally to the White House and has stopped publishing safety research (AP, 2026-11-08); Amazon formed a home-robotics team for a "new-to-world robot product" (CNBC, 2026-11-08); and China's 1,000-km hollow-core fibre trial plus PJM's $11.11/MWh data-centre cost estimate.
